name: Pagecloud
summary: AI website builder for small businesses: describe your business and Pagecloud AI builds the site, which you edit by chat or on the page, with inquiry forms, privacy-first analytics, SEO settings and hosting included.
best_for: small businesses, consultants and creatives who want a brochure site with inquiry forms, built and edited by chatting with Pagecloud AI, with hosting and analytics in one bill
skip_if: you want a native blog or online store, which Pagecloud AI does not currently include on any of its three plans (pricing FAQ, read 12 October 2026), or you need to know your AI allowance in numbers before you pay
honest_knock: Pagecloud AI has no native blog or online store; the pricing FAQ, read on 12 October 2026, says Pagecloud AI does not currently include native blogging or ecommerce, so on Launch, Grow and Optimize you embed or link an outside service. The plans are separated by AI usage that the page gives only as multipliers with no numbers, and AI is free 'for typical use' during a beta, so what you will pay for AI once the beta ends is not on the page. Launch includes no team members. The older Pagecloud Classic builder is kept for existing customers only (llms.txt, read 25 October 2026), so this review covers only the Pagecloud AI plans. We have not used Pagecloud ourselves. The terms renew a subscription automatically unless notice is given at least ten days before it ends and say payments are non-refundable; after a suspension or termination Pagecloud says it will try to help you retrieve data within 10 days. There is no import of an existing site yet.

pricing.entry_price_terms: Launch · per month equivalent billed annually
pricing.notes: (read 2026-10-11 on pagecloud.com/pricing, USD, with the monthly and annual toggle and the FAQ opened) Three plans, each with Pagecloud AI, hosting, SSL, your own domain, inquiry forms with an inbox, analytics and SEO settings. Billed annually and shown as a monthly equivalent: Launch $22, Grow $36, Optimize $69. Billed monthly: Launch $26, Grow $45, Optimize $89. The plans differ only in AI usage and team members: Launch has 'some AI usage' and no team members, Grow twice the AI usage and up to 10 team members, Optimize five times and up to 100. The page says these are relative allowances, not a guaranteed number of pages or requests, and that numerical allowances are not specified; extra AI credits are sold in bundles, without a price on the page. Monthly plans get a fresh allowance each month; annual plans receive the year's allowance up front. Annual plans add a free custom domain (up to a $20 value) and one year of Google Workspace for one user (an $82 value). The FAQ says Pagecloud AI is in beta and normal AI usage is not charged during the beta, though excessive use may be rate-limited, and that it does not include native blogging or ecommerce: you link to an external service or embed its code. Re-read on 25 October 2026 with a plain fetch of pagecloud.com/pricing and Pagecloud's llms.txt: prices, AI multipliers, team limits and the annual extras unchanged, and the page still says Free to create during the beta. The terms of service renew a subscription for another one or twelve months unless notice is given at least ten days before it ends, and say payments are non-refundable even if you stop using the Services.

compare_with.name: Weblium
compare_with.why: Weblium is in our dossiers too: a template builder with a free plan, where the online store, blog and multilingual pages come with its Business plan. Pagecloud AI builds the site from a conversation and, per its pricing FAQ read on 12 October 2026, does not currently include a native blog or store on any of its three plans. If you plan to sell or publish articles, Weblium covers that natively and Pagecloud AI does not; if you want the AI to do the building, Pagecloud AI is the one designed for it. Pagecloud's older Classic builder has its own blog and store tools, but its llms.txt says Classic remains available to existing customers, so this comparison is with Pagecloud AI.

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 30 October 2026 in the free early access beta: Daan created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. We asked the AI builder for a one-page site with two sections of our test text and looked for an export. We did not publish the site.
findings: Building was free during the beta, with no card.
The AI builder only starts if you tick 'I give permission for Pagecloud to review my AI editor sessions and collect usage data'. Until then the send button stays disabled.
The assistant summed up our request and said our two section headings and text 'will be used as written'. The finished page did not contain them; it had its own placeholder sections instead.
Building the site took about six minutes.
We found no way to download or export the site in the project and dashboard menus.
sessions.note: Findings as written up after the session; no pass/fail per task was scored.
